conviction_note: The main evidence is the company's own seasonality. Q3 revenue ran about 5% above underlying Q2 revenue in both 2024 and 2025. Q2 2026 underlying revenue was $180.8m, so the same step points to about $186-189m against a consensus of $179-183m, and management said it is aiming for the top of its guide. A rising short position (about 11% of shares out, 7.7 days to cover) into a stock down 7.5% in five days adds to the upside. The pull the other way is a Q4 euro headwind against a guide built at the June 30 exchange rate, plus put/call skew that already pays for upside. p_up 60 x abs 13 gives +2.6. The finding sum (+2.6) and the scaled number agree.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus is about $182-183m and EPS about -$0.21. Sources: Earnings Whispers preview, $183.3m / -$0.21 (https://finviz.com/news/405714/novocure-must-show-its-breakout-second-quarter-was-a-trend-not-a-one-off); Benzinga, $182.4m (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVCR/earnings). Lower prints elsewhere: Chartmill $179.9m and the Earnings Whispers stock page $179.27m. The FY26 company guide is $710-725m, raised on 2026-07-23 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001645113/000164511326000063/nvcr-20260630xpr.htm). H1 was about $357.7m, which implies $176-184m a quarter in H2. FY consensus is $712.4m, near the low end of the guide. The revenue bar is sourced to two roughly agreeing estimates plus the company guide. The $4m spread between sources still caps how precise the beat call can be.
positioning_check: Short interest per Equibles/FINRA (https://equibles.com/stocks/nvcr/shortinterest): 12.82m shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, up 1.66m from 11.16m on 09-30. That is about 11% of 116.45m shares outstanding, the highest in the window back to June. Days to cover 7.71. Benzinga on 2026-09-29 showed 13.7% of float and 11.48 days. The baseline 25-delta skew is -27.98 vol points: 25-delta calls are bid well over puts, so upside is paid. Put/call OI is 0.74. Total OI is only 2,360 and the ATM spread is 59% of mid, so the implied move (11.06% event) is indicative only. Tape: -7.5% over 5 days, -9.6% over 20 days, -27.9% from the 52-week high. The last two prints moved +27.5% and +28.4%.

findings.finding: Company releases show Q3 revenue ran about 5% above underlying Q2 revenue in each of the last two years. 2024: Q2 $150.4m less $7.6m one-time = $142.8m, against Q3 $155.1m less $4.7m one-time = $150.4m (+5.3%). 2025: Q2 $158.8m against Q3 $167.2m (+5.3%, including some euro tailwind). Q2 2026 was $183.6m less $2.8m one-time = $180.8m underlying. A ~4% step, net of a ~1% q/q euro headwind, gives about $186-189m against a $179-183m consensus. Consensus sits near flat-to-Q2 because management said the top of the guide is 'roughly in line with Q2', and management also said it is 'aiming for the high end'. Gio actives grew 11% y/y and Pax actives were 285 and rising at June 30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has paid for revenue beats lately. Q2 2026 beat ($183.6m vs about $174m) with a raise and moved +28.4%. Q1 2026 moved +27.5%. Q4 2025 revenue missed and the stock fell 8.3%. Q2 2025 fell 24%.
findings.why_not_priced: Every preview anchors Q3 near Q2 ($179-183m). The Earnings Whispers preview calls $183.3m 'essentially flat' with Q2. That anchoring follows management's call remark that the high end of the guide is roughly the Q2 run rate. If the market expected the usual Q3 seasonal step, consensus would sit at $186m+ and FY consensus would be above the guide midpoint, not at $712.4m near its low end.
findings.independence: Q3 2024 and Q2 2024 are from separate company releases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1645113/000164511324000033/nvcr-20240930xpr1.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1645113/000164511324000018/nvcr-20240630xpr.htm). Q3 2025 is at https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251030825661/en/Novocure-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results. 'Aiming for the high end' is from the Q2 call transcript (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2937208). This is an inference from the company's own history, not a reported Q3 number.

findings.finding: Euro moves cut against both the quarter and the guide. Per poundsterlinglive daily data, EUR/USD averaged about 1.152 in Q3 2026 against about 1.164 in Q2, roughly -1% q/q on about $60m of euro-area revenue (Germany $23.3m and France $21.3m in Q2). It closed at 1.1122 on 2026-10-28, 2.6% below the 1.1422 of June 30 that the FY guide assumes. That is about $1.5-2m of Q4 revenue headwind and trims room to raise the top end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX has not been the stated driver of any recent reaction. Q3 2025 cited $3.3m of FX benefit inside an 8% growth quarter, and the stock fell 4.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 move is recent: the euro fell from 1.133 on Sep 30 to 1.112 now. Consensus FY revenue of $712.4m was set mostly before that. If it were priced, previews would flag an FX cut to the guide, and none found do.
findings.independence: The guide's FX basis (June 30 rates) is from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001645113/000164511326000063/nvcr-20260630xpr.htm). The rate path is a macro proxy that the company has not confirmed.

findings.finding: Short interest is building into the print: 12.82m shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement (about 11% of shares outstanding), up 1.66m from Sep 30 and the highest since at least June, with 7.7 days to cover. Meanwhile the stock fell 7.5% in five days to $14.42. The last two prints moved +27.5% and +28.4% on beat-and-raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two most recent beats squeezed +27-28% on event-day volume 7-8x the 20-day median, which is consistent with short covering.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The -28 vol point skew already says calls are bid. What may not be priced is the size of the squeeze on a beat, with the short at a local high and 7.7 days to cover. A positive finding that agrees with the skew is sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: The baseline skew (-27.98, upside paid) and the 5-day run-up of -7.5% are a separate source pointing the same way. Short-interest figures differ between Benzinga (13.7%, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/nvcr) and Equibles.

findings.finding: Q2 gross margin of 78% included a one-time $4.9m tariff refund. Management guided mid-70s gross margin through year-end, because Pax patients are treated before broad reimbursement (Pax recognized revenue was only $1.6m against 285 actives). A lower Q3 margin and a wider loss (consensus -$0.21 vs -$0.13 in Q2) are expected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin has not been the driver of recent moves. The Q3 2025 margin fell to 73% and the stock moved -4.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. This sits inside guidance and the EPS consensus already steps down. It matters only if margin falls below the mid-70s.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K states the $4.9m refund and the mid-70s margin assumption (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001645113/000164511326000063/nvcr-20260630xpr.htm). That is the same company source as the transcript.

findings.finding: Japan's MHLW approved Optune Pax for unresectable locally advanced pancreatic cancer (8-K, 2026-10-01). It is the third approval after the US (Feb 2026) and the EU (CE Mark, June 2026). Japan already has national Lua reimbursement, and the call may update Japan launch timing or the Lua+Pax $20-30m range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell about 5% on 2026-10-02, the day after the approval, so this approval was not bought.
findings.why_not_priced: The approval is public and priced. Any value is in a launch or reimbursement timeline first given on the call.

findings.finding: An 8-K (Item 8.01, 2026-09-01) disclosed unauthorized access to a subsidiary's systems in mid-August 2026. It exposed internal patient IDs for over 1,400 US patients and identifying data for fewer than 50 patients. The company says it is not material and operations are unaffected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. This is the first disclosed incident.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for eight weeks and declared not material. It matters only if the 10-Q quantifies costs or an Item 1.05 amendment appears.

findings.finding: Full TRIDENT data were presented at ASTRO 2026 (Medscape, 2026-10-09). The ITT survival miss is confirmed (17.7 vs 17.5 months, HR 0.953), and only an exploratory MGMT-methylated subgroup signal emerged. The Gio label stays unchanged, so the earlier-use expansion of the core franchise is off the table.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The topline on 2026-06-18 cost about 10-20% intraday. The next print, Q2, still moved +28%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced since June. It enters only if management changes its Gio growth framing on the call.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-28, the day before the print, Novocure announced a clinical trial collaboration and supply agreement to test TTFields with VS-7375, an oral KRAS G12D inhibitor, in pancreatic cancer. About 25 patients, enrolling from 2027. This is the RAS-inhibitor partnering the Q2 preview flagged as a catalyst.
findings.why_not_priced: Announced the day before the print and very small (25 patients, 2027 start). It may get airtime on the call as pipeline support for Pax.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview names RAS-inhibitor partners as a watched item (https://finviz.com/news/405714/novocure-must-show-its-breakout-second-quarter-was-a-trend-not-a-one-off).

outside_window.finding: The FDA decision on the Optune Mya PMA (brain metastases from NSCLC, METIS) is guided for Q4 2026. No decision was found as of 2026-10-28. It could come with the print or later in Q4, and its date is unknown.
KEYNOTE D58 (newly diagnosed GBM with pembrolizumab) completes enrollment in Q4 2026. It is an operational milestone with no data in the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Q3 2026 Optune Pax prescription or active-patient data from any third party: none found; the last data point is 418 Rx and 285 actives at Q2

Medicare/DME MAC coverage decision or proposed LCD for Pax: none found; existing LCD L34823 covers GBM only (https://www.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/details/lcd-details.aspx?LCDId=34823), and Cigna policy effective 2026-09-15 excludes non-GBM indications (https://static.cigna.com/assets/chcp/pdf/coveragePolicies/medical/mm_Future/mm_0581_coveragepositioncriteria_therabionic.pdf)
Any FDA approval of Optune Mya before the print: none found
Analyst rating or price-target changes in October 2026: none dated found (MarketBeat avg PT $21.20 per ad-hoc-news 2026-10-20)
Cause of the -7.5% 5-day drop: no company news found besides the 10-28 VS-7375 collaboration; treated as no cause (worth 0)
Company IR news page: investor.novocure.com returned 403; EDGAR submissions used instead (8-Ks 09-01, 09-09, 10-01 since Q2)
Japan Lua/Pax reimbursement updates after October 1: none found

rejected_candidates.candidate: Director Timothy Scannell retired from the board effective 2026-09-02, with no disagreement stated (8-K Item 5.02)
rejected_candidates.detail: The filing itself states the retirement involved no disagreement, and there is no line it could land on in the print. Not one of the four drop reasons in strict terms; it is listed here so the panel can see it and is worth about 0.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q2 2026 Pax: about half of prescribers wrote only one script, and management targeted repeat prescribing in Q3
rejected_candidates.detail: Folded into the seasonality/revenue finding (finding 1) and the margin finding (finding 4). No Q3 Pax data exists to size it separately.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the skew, which pays for upside, and with the setup (a 5-day selloff into a rising short). The positive lean is therefore partly priced, and the positioning finding was sized small for that.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (a macro proxy without company confirmation is filed small): FX finding cut from -0.7 to -0.5.
Lesson 7 / core table (a finding that agrees with a strong skew is partly priced): positioning finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7.
Lesson 6 (a finding inside what the company already guided goes toward 0): mid-70s gross-margin finding cut from -0.3 to -0.1.

Lesson 1 checked against reaction history: the last two beats paid +27-28%, so the seasonality finding stays at +2.5. Lesson 6 bar check: two estimate sources roughly agree ($182.4m / $183.3m) plus the company guide, so no cap beyond the existing range.
